description_full: Reddit, Inc. operates a digital community in the United States and internationally. The company's platform enables user to engage in conversations, explore passions, research new hobbies, exchange goods and services, create new communities and experiences, share laughs, and find belonging. It also organizes communities based on specific interests that enable users to engage in conversations by sharing experiences, submitting links, uploading images and videos, and replying to one another. Reddit, Inc. was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
ceo_bio: Mr. Steven Ladd Huffman | Co-Founder, CEO, President & Director | Age 41 | Compensation: $3.1M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 2K people. Revenue per employee of $862K ranks in the above the sector median among Communication Services peers. Each employee generates $268K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $134K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (10/10).
financial_summary: Reddit, Inc. is a large-cap communication services business with a $18.4B market cap on $2.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +69% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +63.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -37% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $684M in free cash flow — roughly 31 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.30× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and stock-based comp at 16% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 20% operating margin runs 11pp above the Communication Services median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.98x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 19% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 64% below the high.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $45.33 (margin of safety -110%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 11%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $34.41 to $62.28 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Communication Services peers: P/E 19.4 vs 14.9, EV/EBITDA 16.3 vs 9.4 and P/FCF 26.8 vs 11.3 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.7% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 29 covering analysts target $154 on average, 62% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 37% falls short of the cost of capital of 11.1%, so growth at these returns destroys value.
It converts 31% of revenue into free cash flow, or 15% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.30x.
ROE of 18% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.1x equity multiplier).
It spends 35.6% of revenue on R&D and 15.6% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.5B (5% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 69.4% over 3 years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.95, a backlog worth 7% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 22%.
Capex runs only 0.4x depreciation (0.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 36.9% on average.
Analysts expect 20.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.7%), and institutions hold 93%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (55 sales, net $34.1M sold).
Short interest is elevated at 14.8% of the float, 4.6 days to cover.
people: With about 2,555 employees, each generates about $862K of revenue, 1.4x the Communication Services median.
That works out to $268K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $3.1M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
